story_type: heavy-lift helicopter sling-loads a stranded 11,800-pound buoy off a beach
hook: A storm threw this 11,800 pound buoy onto a beach.
narration: This navigation buoy weighs eleven thousand eight hundred pounds, and a helicopter is lifting it off a beach.
A winter storm in twenty ten tore it free from its mooring and washed it ashore at La Push, Washington.
By August twenty eleven it was still sitting on the sand near the mouth of the Quillayute River.
So the Coast Guard called in an Army Chinook from Joint Base Lewis McChord.
It landed right on the beach beside the buoy.
A Chinook has two big rotors that spin in opposite directions, so it needs no tail rotor and puts its power into lifting.
Crews hooked the buoy to a long line under the helicopter. [short pause] Then the line went tight.
The buoy rose off the sand, past the cliffs, and out over the surf.
outcome: The Chinook carried the buoy away from the beach and out over the Pacific.
title: 11,800 pound buoy lifted off a beach
description:
On Aug. 29, 2011, Coast Guard Thirteenth District members and an Army Chinook helicopter from Joint Base Lewis-McChord removed an 11,800-pound navigation buoy from a beach near the Quillayute River mouth in La Push, Washington. The buoy had washed ashore after breaking free from its mooring in a 2010 winter storm.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Nathan W. Bradshaw, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/317190/buoy-hoist-la-push
